write.prompt: Some Vietnamese families now send their children abroad at the age of fifteen or sixteen to finish upper secondary school. Do the benefits of this choice outweigh its drawbacks?
write.taskVi: essay 4 đoạn, 200–250 từ: mở bài có thesis trả lời "outweigh" – lợi ích – bất lợi (có câu cân nhắc) – kết bài.
mustUse: một so sánh có mức độ
một câu với outweigh / be offset by / at the cost of
write.modelAfterSubmit:
In recent years, some Vietnamese families have started sending their children abroad at the age of fifteen or sixteen to finish upper secondary school. Although this trend offers real benefits, I believe that for most teenagers of this age the disadvantages outweigh the advantages.

Admittedly, studying abroad early can broaden a young person's horizons. By using English every day, teenagers usually become far more fluent than their friends at home, and they learn to solve everyday problems without their parents' help. Some schools abroad also offer subjects and activities that are not available in Vietnam.

However, these benefits often come at a high cost. Tuition fees and the cost of living abroad are much higher than at home, which puts heavy pressure on many families. More importantly, a sixteen-year-old is still developing emotionally. Without a support network nearby, many young students suffer from homesickness and culture shock, and some fall behind because no one notices their problems early. These difficulties are not easily offset by better language skills.

In conclusion, sending teenagers abroad for upper secondary school can broaden their horizons, but the financial and emotional costs are usually greater. In my view, most students would gain far more from studying abroad at university, when they are mature enough to adapt.
